saltline.goal: Build an original first-person 3D tactical shooter set in a rain-soaked automated cargo port at night. Formula: "The player feels like a lone, outnumbered saboteur who wins by nerve and positioning because the game keeps pushing small packs of fast machines at them between pockets of steel cover and short breathers." The hook is atmosphere plus a short, finishable mission: three objectives, one extraction, about five minutes.
saltline.controls: Desktop: click the canvas once to capture the mouse (pointer lock), WASD move, mouse look, left click fire, right click aim down sights, R reload, Q swap to sidearm, E hold-to-interact on objectives, Space jump, Shift sprint, C crouch, Esc pause (pause must release the mouse; Resume recaptures it). Gamepad: sticks move/look, RT fire, LT aim, X reload/interact, Y sidearm. Touch: left-thumb virtual stick moves, right-thumb drag looks, on-screen Fire, Aim, Reload, Jump and Interact buttons; detect touch and show the touch layout automatically. If pointer lock is refused (sandboxed iframe), fall back to drag-to-look.
saltline.camera: First-person, ~75 degree FOV that narrows to ~55 when aiming; procedural weapon view-model with sway, recoil kick and reload animation; light head-bob while sprinting, small camera shake on taking damage; fog and rain reduce long sight lines so threats appear at 20-40 m.
saltline.rules: Two modes. Mission: disable 3 data relays spread across the yard (hold E for ~3 s each while exposed), each relay cut escalates enemy waves; after the third, run to an extraction boat at the quay; win = reach the boat, lose = health reaches 0. Holdout: endless escalating waves with a resupply pause between waves; score = time survived and machines destroyed, track best score in localStorage. Enemies: fast four-legged ground drones that rush and melee, and small flying drones that strafe from above; introduce ground units first, flyers after the first relay. Difficulty selector (Standard / Hard / Brutal) scales enemy count, damage and accuracy. Health regenerates slowly behind cover; ammo is finite per magazine with reserve pickups. Death screen shows time, objectives done, kills and a one-click Retry; win screen shows rating, time, accuracy and Redeploy. Pause menu: Resume, Settings (quality low/medium/high), Controls, Restart.
saltline.art: Grounded industrial realism rendered in real-time 3D with physically based materials; blocky shipping containers, gantry cranes, chain-link fences and pipe racks with chunky readable silhouettes. Palette: wet asphalt greys and rust browns for the environment, bone-white HUD text, one warm amber signal colour for objectives and interactables, cold cyan glow for hostile machines. Night rain under sodium floodlights, wet reflections, drifting fog and mist. First-person perspective, high contrast between lit cover and dark lanes keeps enemies legible.
saltline.assets: Everything procedural in code by default, no external downloads: containers, cranes, quay, fences and drones built from Three.js primitives and merged/instanced geometry; textures (rust, paint, stencil labels, signage, wet asphalt) drawn to CanvasTexture at load; rain and tracers as instanced particles. Invent fictional company names and stencil text for signage. Optional: up to 2 generated images (title key art and a menu background) only after the user approves cost; no CC0 model pack needed. Budget: $0 required, generation cap 2 images. Keep the single page under ~4 MB.
saltline.audio: All Web Audio, synthesized: layered gunshot (noise burst + low thump + tail), reload clicks, footsteps on metal vs asphalt, drone servo whine and rotor buzz with positional panning, rain and distant harbour horn ambience, a low minor-key drone pad that intensifies during waves. Start AudioContext on the first click, provide mute and master volume in Settings, cap simultaneous shots.
acceptance: Title screen states the mission in one sentence and the Deploy button starts play in 1 click; within 3 seconds of spawning the player sees the first objective marker and a controls legend.
Pointer lock works on desktop; Esc pauses and releases the mouse; Resume recaptures it; drag-to-look fallback works when lock is refused.
A full Mission run (3 relays + extraction) is completable on Standard in 4-8 minutes; Holdout waves visibly escalate and resupply between waves.
Death shows a stats card with one-click Retry that restarts without reloading the page; win shows a debrief with time and accuracy.
Holds 60 fps at 1280x720 on a mid-range laptop with Medium quality; a Low preset exists for weak devices.
Touch layout appears automatically on phones and every action is reachable without a keyboard.
No external asset requests besides the Three.js CDN; no console errors during a full run.
saltline.originality: Already an original concept, keep it that way: do not reuse the name 'Saltline', the 'Harbormaster' AI, 'Berth 4', or the original signage text; invent your own port name, faction, enemy names and mission copy. Do not copy any code from the reference artifact. Optionally shift the setting (e.g. oil rig, airport cargo apron, rail yard) if the user wants distance from the reference.

little-prince.goal: Build an original, gentle 3D story-exploration game about a small traveller hopping between tiny storybook planets. Formula: "The player feels quiet wonder and tenderness because the game keeps revealing a new hand-painted miniature world, each with one strange inhabitant and one small kindness to perform." No combat; the reward is discovery and a short poetic line of story on each world.
little-prince.controls: Desktop: WASD/arrow keys walk around the curved planet surface, mouse drag orbits the camera, Space jump, E talk/interact, Enter advance dialogue, M open the star map to travel to the next planet, Esc pause. Touch: left virtual stick walks, one-finger drag on the right side orbits, tap an inhabitant or object to interact, tap dialogue to advance, a map button for travel. Click/tap anywhere on the title to begin (also unlocks audio).
little-prince.camera: Third-person orbit camera that keeps the whole tiny planet partly in frame (the curvature is the charm); gravity points to each planet's centre so the character walks all the way around; camera auto-reorients 'up' smoothly. Travel between planets is a short cinematic fly-through over a starfield, then a slow descent. Title screen shows a planet slowly rotating.
little-prince.rules: Loop: land on a planet -> explore -> meet its single inhabitant -> complete one small task (water a flower, light a lamp, find a lost object, listen to a story) -> receive a star fragment -> unlock the next planet on the star map. 5-7 planets, each 3-5 minutes; teach walking on the first planet with no task pressure. No fail state; optional collectibles (hidden flowers) for completionists. Ending: return to the home planet for a closing scene, then 'Begin again' restarts; progress per planet saved in localStorage with a Reset option. Bilingual text (English + Chinese) is a plus.
little-prince.art: Soft watercolour storybook rendered in real-time 3D: small spherical planets with rounded, slightly lumpy hand-shaped forms, visible paper grain and brush-edge textures. Palette: deep indigo night sky with warm gold stars for the environment, a cream-and-saffron traveller as the hero colour, single saturated coral accents marking interactable objects. Warm low key light with soft rim glow, gentle bloom and floating dust. Third-person view framing the whole curved miniature world.
little-prince.assets: Planets, props and the hero as low-poly procedural or simple modelled meshes with a watercolour shader (paper-grain noise, posterized lighting, edge darkening) done in code. Allowed: up to 6 generated images (title painting, per-planet painted skybox/backdrop) after cost approval; if the user has a 3D generation tool, up to 7 generated hero/inhabitant models, otherwise build them from primitives. CC0 option: a small stylized character pack (e.g. Quaternius/Kenney) recoloured to the formula. Budget cap: $15 of generation unless the user approves more. Provide a WebGL2 path; WebGPU is optional, never required.
little-prince.audio: Soft piano/celesta music loop per planet (generated if approved, otherwise a simple Web Audio arpeggio pad), gentle footstep chimes, a twinkle on interactables, page-turn sound on dialogue, wind on travel. No voice required. Mute toggle and volume slider.
acceptance: First playable frame within 5 seconds on a mid-range laptop with a visible loading percentage that never stalls silently; an explicit message if WebGL2/WebGPU is unavailable.
Within 3 seconds on the first planet the player knows to walk and look for the glowing interactable (on-screen hint).
Character can walk the full circumference of each planet without falling off or camera flipping.
Each planet's task can be completed and unlocks travel; the full journey is completable in 15-30 minutes.
55-60 fps on a 2020-era laptop with integrated graphics using the WebGL2 path.
Touch controls work on a phone in landscape; all text readable at 375 px width.
Restart/'Begin again' resets the journey without a page reload; progress persists across reloads.
little-prince.originality: The reference adapts a copyrighted book IP; do not use its title, the prince, the rose, the fox, the baobabs, the lamplighter, the king, the asteroid name or any of its text or illustrations. Invent a new protagonist (e.g. a small lantern-keeper or a paper-boat child), a new reason to travel (collect star fragments to relight a sky), new inhabitants with their own quirks (a lighthouse keeper with no sea, a gardener of clocks, a cartographer of clouds), and new written dialogue. Name the game something original. Keep the watercolour mood but use your own palette and motifs.
sourceNotes: Original post (@Saccc_c, X, 2026-10-13, 3.92M views): 16 days with Opus 5.5 + Tripo (3D model generation) + Blender; each planet in the story is an explorable 3D scene; author plans to open-source later (not yet).

sky-reach.goal: Build an original seamless space-to-surface exploration game. Formula: "The player feels the scale and freedom of a whole small galaxy because the game keeps letting them fly from orbit straight down to a planet's surface, land, and step out on foot without a loading screen." Lead with flight feel and the seamless descent; light objectives give direction.
sky-reach.controls: Desktop flight: W/S throttle, mouse steers pitch/yaw (pointer lock), A/D roll, Shift boost, Space ascend / L land when near ground, F exit/enter ship, Esc pause. On foot: WASD walk, mouse look, Space jump, E interact/collect. Touch: left stick = pitch/yaw (or walk), right side = throttle slider and Boost, Land/Exit buttons. Gamepad optional.
sky-reach.camera: Third-person chase camera behind the ship with speed-based FOV widening and slight lag in turns; switches to third-person over-the-shoulder on foot. The atmosphere entry uses a short heat/fog transition. Use a floating origin (re-centre the world around the player) so huge distances do not jitter.
sky-reach.rules: Goal: recover 3-5 warp cores to repair the ship. Loop: pick a beacon (vertical light beam visible from orbit) -> fly to its planet -> descend -> land near the beam -> explore on foot -> collect the core (small hazard: hostile drones or a terrain puzzle) -> return to ship. 3-5 hand-tuned planets with distinct biomes generated from seeds (grassland with rock arches, desert, ice, ocean islands), not 80. HUD: speed, altitude, hull, fuel, boost meter. Fuel refills on landing pads; hull damage from crashes. Lose = hull 0 -> respawn at last landing with a one-click Retry. Win = all cores, ending flight sequence, then 'New Voyage'.
sky-reach.art: Bright cinematic sci-fi realism rendered in real-time 3D: smooth rolling terrain, tall weathered rock arches and spires, a chunky white hull ship with panel lines. Palette: muted sage greens and sandy ochres for terrain, a white-and-signal-orange ship as the hero, electric cyan light beams marking goals, magenta for hostiles. Hazy daylight with atmospheric scattering and a giant ringed planet on the horizon. Third-person chase perspective, horizon always visible for orientation.
sky-reach.assets: Terrain as procedural heightfield chunks with LOD and biome colour ramps in shaders; sky via scattering shader; rocks, arches and props procedural. Ship: build from primitives, or use one CC0 low-poly spaceship model (Quaternius/Kenney) recoloured to the formula. Optional generated images: 1 key art cover and up to 3 skybox/planet backdrop textures after cost approval. Budget cap $10 generation; no paid 3D generation required.
sky-reach.audio: Synthesized engine hum whose pitch follows throttle, boost whoosh, wind rush that grows with speed in atmosphere, landing thud, pickup chime, ambient synth pad per biome (generated music optional with approval). Mute and volume in pause menu.
acceptance: Title explains 'repair your ship: recover the warp cores' and the first beacon is visible within 3 seconds of launch.
Flying from orbit to landing on a planet has no loading screen and no visible floating-point jitter at the farthest distance.
The player can exit the ship, walk, collect a core and re-enter in under 2 minutes on the first planet.
Holds 50-60 fps on a mid-range laptop with terrain LOD; a quality toggle exists; first playable frame within 8 seconds.
Crash/hull 0 shows a Retry that respawns at the last landing in one click.
Touch controls let a phone player fly, land and walk.
Full run (all cores) completable in 15-25 minutes.
sky-reach.originality: Reference is pitched as 'No Man's Sky'-like; do not use that name, its multi-tool, its UI layout, ship designs, creature designs or the reference game's name 'Sky Reach', its 'Elysia' planet or story text. Invent your own ship, galaxy, faction and planet names and your own objective framing.

shipwreck.goal: Build an original short underwater discovery-and-puzzle game about recovering pieces of an ancient mechanism from a wreck. Formula: "The player feels the hush and curiosity of a lone diver because the game keeps rewarding careful looking - sonar pings, half-buried shapes, brushing silt away - against a gently ticking air supply." Ends with assembling the pieces into a working machine.
shipwreck.controls: Desktop: click to capture mouse, WASD swim/walk on the seabed, mouse look, Space (hold) float upward, Q sonar ping, F hold to face the nearest marker, E hold (or click-drag) to brush silt off a find, 1-3 pick a recovered part and Enter to fit it in the assembly scene, Esc pause. Touch: left thumb walks, swipe to look, buttons for Jump/Float, Sonar and Brush; brushing by rubbing a finger on the object.
shipwreck.camera: First-person diver view with slow bob, soft depth-of-field and caustic light ripples; turbidity fog limits sight to ~15-25 m so sonar matters. During the assembly finale switch to a close orbit view of the mechanism with drag-to-rotate.
shipwreck.rules: Find 3 fragments in a compact wreck area. Air timer starts at 2:00 per dive (refillable at an air hose/anchor line); depth readout; leaving the play area triggers 'too deep / hose reaches no farther' warnings. Sonar ping briefly reveals the direction of the nearest unfound piece with an audio cue; at the piece, hold Brush to clean and reveal it (progress ring). Each piece reveals a one-line historical-style clue. After all 3: puzzle scene - place 3 gears/plates in the right slots using clues (tooth counts, symbols); wrong fits give a gentle hint. Air out = hauled to the boat, restart the dive keeping found pieces. Win screen: 'found in mm:ss' + 'Dive again'. Target 8-15 minutes.
shipwreck.art: Painterly underwater realism rendered in real-time 3D: soft rounded rocks, swaying seagrass ribbons, encrusted timber ribs and corroded bronze with crisp gear teeth. Palette: deep teal and blue-green murk for the environment, warm verdigris-gold bronze as the hero colour, bright coral and fish schools as accent life, a white sonar ring as the signal. Sunbeam god-rays and caustics from above fading into dark depth. First-person diver perspective; finds glint subtly.
shipwreck.assets: All procedural in code: terrain, rocks, seagrass (instanced, thousands), fish schools (instanced boids, aim for 1,000-2,000 on desktop, scale down on mobile), wreck timbers, amphorae, and the gear mechanism (procedural gear geometry with real tooth counts). Caustics and fog via shaders. Fonts: a classical serif. Optional: 1 generated title painting after cost approval. Budget $0 required, $5 cap. Single HTML page target <= 4 MB.
shipwreck.audio: Procedural Web Audio: muffled underwater ambience (filtered noise), diver breathing tied to air level (faster when low), bubble bursts, sonar ping with echo, brushing scrape, metallic gear clicks in the finale, a sparse modal music bed swelling at each find. Mute toggle.
acceptance: Title states the premise in one sentence with 'Begin the dive'; within 3 seconds underwater the HUD shows air, depth and 'Find the three fragments'.
Sonar ping clearly points toward an unfound piece; every piece is findable without a guide.
Air reaching 0 returns the player to the surface and lets them dive again in one click without losing found pieces.
Assembly puzzle accepts the correct solution and rejects wrong fits with a hint; win screen shows time and 'Dive again'.
Holds 60 fps on a mid-range laptop and >=30 fps on a recent phone (auto-reduce fish/grass counts).
Full touch play possible including brushing.
No external requests other than the Three.js CDN.
shipwreck.originality: The reference is an original concept around a real historical artefact (public domain history). To be clearly distinct: do not reuse the title 'Antikythera', its Greek loading lines, its on-screen copy, or the exact three-fragment clue texts; pick either a different real or fictional relic (e.g. a lost star-compass, a bronze tide-calculator from an invented culture) and write your own clues. Do not copy any code from the artifact.

turbo-kart.goal: Build an original arcade kart racer with a full race-day presentation. Formula: "The player feels the joy of a tight comeback because the game keeps feeding drift-boost skill and position-weighted item luck into a pack of rubber-banded rivals." Polish (title demo race, countdown, results) is part of the effect.
turbo-kart.controls: Desktop: W/Up accelerate, S/Down brake/reverse, A/D or Left/Right steer, Space hop and hold to drift, E or Shift use item, C look back, Esc/P pause, M mute; Enter/click on menus. Gamepad: A/RT accelerate, B/LT brake, stick steer, RB drift, LB item. Touch (the reference has none; add it): auto-accelerate toggle or right-side gas pedal, left-side steering zone (drag or tilt option), Drift and Item buttons.
turbo-kart.camera: Third-person spring-damped chase camera ~6.5 m behind and ~2.6 m above the kart, FOV 70 widening to ~84 at top speed/boost, swing into drifts, small shake on hits; pre-race flyover of the track, rear-view on look-back.
turbo-kart.rules: 8 racers (player + 7 AI) on one closed circuit, 3 laps (selectable 1-5), class/difficulty 50/100/150 equivalent. Drift-charge: holding drift through a corner charges 3 spark levels (thresholds ~0.9 s / 1.9 s / 3.0 s) for increasing mini-boosts; hold accelerate at GO for a rocket start. Track has boost pads, 1-2 jump ramps (trick boost), off-road slowdown, item box rows. 6-8 items with odds weighted by race position (back of pack gets stronger items). AI follows a racing line, drifts, uses items and rubber-bands. HUD: lap, timer, position list, item roulette, minimap, speedometer, final-lap banner, wrong-way warning. Results screen with placings and Restart / Change racer. Live demo race behind the title screen.
turbo-kart.art: Bright toy-like low-poly 3D: chunky rounded karts, oversized helmets on stubby drivers, faceted pine trees and angular mountains, candy-striped kerbs. Palette: fresh greens and sky blues for the environment, a saturated primary colour per racer as hero identity, hot pink and gold for items and boost pads. Sunny midday light with soft shadows and gentle bloom. Third-person chase perspective; the road, kerbs and item boxes always read clearly against grass.
turbo-kart.assets: Everything generated in code at load: track spline geometry, kerbs, barriers with fictional sponsor banners, scenery, karts, drivers and item models from primitives; CanvasTexture for asphalt, banners and portraits; pooled particle effects. No external asset files. Optional: 1 generated title key art and 8 racer portrait images after cost approval (cap $5); otherwise render portraits from the 3D models.
turbo-kart.audio: Web Audio only: engine tone tied to speed per kart (player loudest), drift screech, spark-level chimes, boost whoosh, item sounds, crowd cheer at finish; sequenced chiptune music with separate menu and race tracks that speeds up on the final lap. M to mute.
acceptance: Title screen shows 'press Enter / tap to start' and a racer can be on the grid within 3 interactions.
3-2-1-GO countdown, rocket start and 3-level drift boost all work and are visibly signalled by spark colours.
A 3-lap race on normal takes 2.5-4 minutes and the AI finishes in a spread that the player can beat with drifting.
Results screen offers one-click Restart and Change racer without page reload.
60 fps at 1280x720 on a mid-range laptop with 8 karts and effects.
Fully playable on a phone with touch controls.
No Nintendo-derived names, item designs or characters anywhere (see originality).
turbo-kart.originality: Reference markets itself as a Mario Kart clone and its post claims Mario and Luigi are playable; its code uses renamed racers but still copies franchise item concepts (mushroom, banana, green/red/blue shell, star, lightning) and look-alike hats (mushroom cap, shell). Replace all of that: invent a new world (e.g. kitchen-utensil racers, desert critters, robot couriers), new racer names and silhouettes with no caps/moustaches/turtle shells, and a new item set with distinct visuals (e.g. spring trap, oil slick, magnet pull, homing paper plane, time-freeze bubble, leader-seeking comet). Rename the game; avoid 'Kart' + Nintendo-style title fonts; no question-mark item boxes - use a different pickup shape.
sourceNotes: Original post (@bridgemindai, X, 2026-09-22, 380K views): 'Claude Opus 5.5 just ONE SHOT a Mario Kart game', claims Mario and Luigi are playable.

Repo README (github.com/bridge-mind/turbo-kart-rally): built by five Opus 5.5 sub-agents from one verbatim prompt asking for a 'triple A quality ... clone of Mario Kart' in Three.js; architecture contract written first (ARCHITECTURE.md), ownership split world / driving / items+FX / art+camera / game+UI; Three.js r170 via import map, no build step, every mesh/texture/sound generated in code.

README/config.js facts: 8 racers with speed/accel/handling/weight stats, ~2.1 km circuit with 8 boost pads, 2 ramps, 30 item boxes; 8 items; drift thresholds 0.9/1.9/3.0 s; difficulty easy/normal/hard with rubber-band 0.08-0.16; chase camera distance 6.5, height 2.6, FOV 70->84 (camera.js).

Live page opened 2026-11-20 in headless Chrome: title 'TURBO KART RALLY - PRESS ENTER / CLICK TO START', character select with 8 racers, class '100cc · NORMAL', '3 LAPS', RACE! button; rAF measured ~61/s in headless; repo race screenshot shows lap timer, position list, minimap, speedometer.
input.js has keyboard and gamepad only - no touch controls (verified in source).

voxel-musou.goal: Build an original voxel 'one-versus-a-thousand' action brawler. Formula: "The player feels overwhelmingly powerful because the game keeps feeding huge crowds of weak soldiers into sweeping combo strings and a screen-clearing special, while a few telegraphed elite captains demand dodging." The spectacle is hundreds of instanced enemies flying apart into voxel debris.
voxel-musou.controls: Desktop: WASD move (camera-relative), J or left click attack (tap for a 6-hit combo), K or right click charge attack (pressed mid-combo branches into different finishers), Space jump (attack in air = air attack), L or Shift dodge, I special when gauge is full, mouse look after clicking the field (pointer lock) or Q/E to rotate camera, R recenter / face nearest captain, Esc pause. Gamepad: X attack, Y charge, A jump, R1 dodge, B special, right stick camera. Touch (reference has none; add it): left stick, Attack, Charge, Dodge, Special buttons, drag right side to rotate camera.
voxel-musou.camera: Third-person behind-and-above camera (~48 degree vertical FOV, ~5.8 m boom at ~17 degrees, hero about a third of frame height); it only rotates when the player asks or slowly realigns while running; never swings on attacks; pulls out in tiers as crowds grow; cinematic short camera choreography during the special; boom avoids walls.
voxel-musou.rules: Fixed-step 60 Hz simulation. Modes: Story (3-4 short stages with objectives: defeat N captains, defend a point for X minutes, escort/rescue, final boss duel) and Trials (e.g. defeat 1,000 soldiers in 3 minutes; hold a bridge 4 minutes; boss gauntlet). Grunts die in one sweep; captains have HP bars, armour and telegraphed wind-ups (40 frames on normal). Special gauge fills from hits; special clears an area. Healing pickups. Difficulty Easy/Normal/Hard/+unlockable Extreme scaling enemy damage, simultaneous attackers and captain HP. Results: rank C-S from KOs, time and damage taken; Retry from results; best rank/time/KOs saved in localStorage. HUD: hero HP, special gauge, combo/chain counter, KO count, captain HP bars, minimap, objective panel.
voxel-musou.art: Chunky voxel diorama rendered in real-time 3D: every character, wall and banner built from crisp cubes with bevelled-looking shading and voxel debris on hits. Palette: dusty ochre ground and smoky umber skies for the battlefield, one bright heroic colour (white and teal armour) for the player, enemy armies in a single cold team colour, gold for special effects and pickups. Golden-hour or dusk light, haze, bloom and depth-of-field. Elevated third-person view keeping the crowd ring readable.
voxel-musou.assets: All procedural: voxel character models defined in code as box lists merged into geometry, soldiers as InstancedMesh (300 default, scalable), voxel castles, terrain, banners with invented emblems; textures via CanvasTexture. Optional: a display font from Google Fonts or a bundled OFL font; up to 2 generated images (title art, stage map) after cost approval, cap $5. Vendor or CDN Three.js only.
voxel-musou.audio: Procedural Web Audio: weapon whoosh and layered hit thuds with hit-stop, crowd shouts, war drums, gong for the special, captain-defeated sting; percussion-heavy music loop per stage (generated music optional with approval). Sound starts on first input; mute toggle.
acceptance: Title -> stage -> fighting in at most 3 interactions; first 3 seconds of a stage show the objective and a control hint bar.
At least 300 enemies on screen at 60 fps on a mid-range laptop; automatic quality reduction under load.
Combo strings, charge branches, dodge and special all work and feel distinct; the special visibly clears the surrounding crowd.
Captain wind-ups are readable and dodgeable; defeat (HP 0 or objective failed) shows a result with one-click Retry.
Results screen shows rank, KOs, time and damage; best records persist after reload.
Full touch play possible on a phone.
Contains no Three Kingdoms names, figures, battles or the 'Musou' term (see originality).
voxel-musou.originality: The reference copies the Dynasty Warriors formula and uses historical Three Kingdoms figures, battles and the series' 'Musou' term and Chinese calligraphic branding. Change: invent a new world (e.g. a mythic archipelago, clockwork kingdom, or a fantasy desert empire) with invented heroes, captains, armies, emblems and battle names; rename the special (e.g. 'Overdrive', 'Storm Break') and the game. Use your own UI typography and colours, not brush-calligraphy title cards; do not reuse the reference's stage list, dialogue or officer move names.
sourceNotes: Original post (@BubuStd, X, 2026-09-24, 170K views): Opus 5.5 'ultracode', inspired by Dynasty Warriors, 'Zhao Yun vs 300 soldiers: combos, dodges, Musou'; stack three.js; repo github.com/mike007jd/voxel-musou.

Repo README: Three.js r186, fixed 60 Hz simulation, plain ES modules, no build; 7 playable officers, 4 story chapters, 3 trials (1,000 KOs in 3 min; hold bridge 4 min; boss gauntlet), 4 difficulties (Chaos unlockable), C-S ranks saved in localStorage; procedural WebAudio; ?enemies=N up to 2000 (default 300).

Source facts: core/input.js keymap J attack, K charge, Space jump, L/Shift dodge, I musou, R target, Q/E camera; keyboard, mouse and gamepad only, no touch; core/difficulty.js windup frames 50/40/35/30 and simultaneous strikers 1/2/2/3; camera/camera.js vFOV 48, boom 5.8 m at 17 degrees.

Live game opened 2026-11-20 in headless Chrome: title and chapter select screens observed; free-battle shortcut (?go=free&char=zhaoyun&map=changban) loaded a battle with hundreds of voxel soldiers; after 6 attack presses + 1 charge the HUD showed a 123-hit chain and 26 KOs, captain HP bars and minimap.
Frame rate on real hardware: unverified.
